bull.b: The licensing and marketing agreements create a scalable commercialization path that can generate royalties and sales-based fees as partner facilities expand. This asset-light structure may allow Loop to monetize its technology and market access without funding every plant directly.

Customer commitments covering more than half of the resized facility provide tangible demand support ahead of construction. If financing is secured, this contracted or committed demand could improve project bankability, reduce commercialization risk, and support earlier capacity utilization.

A process designed to operate at low temperatures and without pressure could support attractive unit economics relative to less efficient recycling methods. Producing virgin-quality materials also broadens potential applications across packaging and textiles, strengthening long-term market relevance.

bear.b: The company has not yet demonstrated stable, scalable operating performance. Very low revenue, negative gross profit, and large operating losses indicate that commercialization remains ahead of recurring earnings generation, leaving results vulnerable to project timing and execution delays.

Continued operating and free-cash-flow deficits mean the business is consuming capital rather than self-funding development. This reduces flexibility to advance projects, increases dependence on external financing, and may force future funding decisions before commercial cash generation is established.

The India project remains dependent on financing that has not been completed, making the expected construction and production timeline uncertain. Delayed or unavailable funding could postpone commercialization, increase financing costs, and prevent Loop from converting customer interest into operating revenue.
